choices.content: Draw a line perpendicular to \(AD\) and prove that two right triangles are congruent
Draw a line through \(D\) parallel to \(AB\) and use the equality of corresponding angles
Take the midpoint \(E\) of \(AB\), join \(DE\), and use the triangle inequality
Extend \(AD\) to \(E\) so that \(DE=AD\), prove \(\triangle ABD\cong\triangle ECD\), and then use the triangle inequality

question.prompt: Given that \(AD\) is a median of \(\triangle ABC\), how can extending the median to twice its length be used to prove \(AB+AC>2AD\)?

solutions.explanation: Extend \(AD\) to \(E\) so that \(DE=AD\), and join \(CE\). Then \(\triangle ABD\cong\triangle ECD\) (SAS), so \(CE=AB\). In \(\triangle ACE\), \(AC+CE>AE=2AD\), giving \(AB+AC>2AD\).
